veracrypt.reason: Upstream distributes Apache-2.0 additions together with inherited TrueCrypt License 3.0 code. TrueCrypt-3.0 is not a current OSI-approved SPDX license; Apache-2.0 alone or LicenseRef is not an acceptable substitute.

logseq.reason: The current upstream README identifies the DB version as beta. A current stable cask version does not by itself establish that this product channel satisfies the stable-release requirement.

bruno.reason: A matching stable cask and Flathub discovery candidate exist, but upstream license retrieval has repeatedly failed with TLS errors. Network failure is not an exclusion; license text and product declaration remain unverified.

zen-browser.reason: MPL-2.0 license text and the upstream cask are identified, but the release uses a b-suffixed version. The upstream stable-channel declaration could not yet be retrieved, so this is not assumed to be a beta or a stable release.

anytype.reason: The upstream Any Source Available License is not a current OSI-approved SPDX license and cannot be replaced by LicenseRef.

aseprite.reason: The distributed Aseprite EULA is not an OSI-approved open-source license, despite the availability of source code.

beekeeper-studio.reason: The desktop cask includes commercially licensed src-commercial portions and a desktop-wide EULA. Only the Community Edition is GPL-3.0-or-later; the complete distributed desktop application has no qualifying all-OSI SPDX expression.

openshot.reason: The cask declares both macOS architectures but resolves both to the same x86_64 DMG. Native aarch64 support is unverified and Rosetta is not assumed; inspect the actual binary or obtain explicit upstream evidence before adding either architecture claim.

vagrant.reason: The stable v2.4.9 package is licensed under BUSL-1.1, which is not OSI-approved. The current development branch's MIT declaration cannot retroactively change the distributed stable package license.

calibre-web.reason: The project is a Python web service deployed through pip/a virtual environment, not an independently installable desktop application through a supported Pakkit package route.

photogimp.reason: The product is a GIMP configuration patch rather than a standalone application, and its generic GPLv3 text/badge does not establish GPL-3.0-only versus GPL-3.0-or-later.

iterm2.reason: Upstream distributes stable macOS archives through its website rather than a supported package-manager or GitHub-release route. No qualifying stable installation method was established.

algermusicplayer.reason: The README imposes a commercial-use restriction in addition to an MIT license file. That field-of-use restriction prevents representing the complete product as OSI MIT.

lantern.reason: Production distribution is verified, but the available declaration and generic GPL text do not distinguish GPL-3.0-only from GPL-3.0-or-later.

pakeplus.reason: Upstream states that the current frontend source is no longer open source. An MIT file and release artifacts do not establish that the complete current product is OSI-licensed.

dearpygui.reason: Dear PyGui is a Python GUI framework/library distributed through PyPI, not an independently installable desktop application through a supported Pakkit package route.

peach.reason: Inspected desktop artifacts are explicitly prereleases/test builds and unsigned. They must not be promoted to stable release variants.

openhuman.reason: Upstream labels the product Early Beta and its cask release is part of that beta channel. A cask version number does not establish stable-product eligibility.

visual-studio-code.reason: The Microsoft-branded Visual Studio Code download is governed by proprietary Microsoft Software License Terms; MIT licensing of the vscode source tree does not cover that product.
visual-studio-code.verifiedLicense: MIT for source; proprietary for the branded product

youtube-dl.reason: No supported stable package-manager or GitHub-release installation path was established; the former Homebrew formula is unavailable.

neovim.reason: The mixed codebase includes Vim-licensed code. Vim is not OSI-approved, so the whole product cannot be represented as Apache-2.0 alone or by an all-OSI SPDX expression.

mole.reason: The formula claims GPL-3.0-or-later but the upstream GPL-3.0 declaration and generic license text do not establish only versus or-later. The separate proprietary Mole for Mac product must not be substituted.

ladybird.reason: Upstream describes Ladybird as pre-alpha and source-build-only; no supported stable package path exists.

easyspider.reason: Releases exist but no supported package-manager route or complete stable GitHub asset mapping was verified.

puter.reason: Puter is a web/self-hosted product; the npm puter.js SDK is not the desktop application and cannot be used as its installation route.

kazumi.reason: The distributed product includes application-icon artwork with separate copying, modification and redistribution restrictions; whole-product redistribution rights are unresolved.

chatbox.reason: The Community Edition package is identified, but upstream GPLv3 wording does not prove GPL-3.0-only versus GPL-3.0-or-later. The proprietary Chatbox package must not be substituted.

vim.reason: The product uses the Vim license, which is not OSI-approved. FSF-libre or GPL-compatible status does not satisfy the catalog requirement.

nw-js.reason: Stable official binaries are hosted on dl.nwjs.io, while GitHub provides source assets only and no authoritative supported package mapping was found.

ocrmypdf.reason: An authoritative Homebrew formula exists but a qualifying stable binary/package route was not established for the intended desktop platform coverage.

shadowsocksx-ng.reason: The current 2.0.0-alpha.2 line is prerelease-only; stable 1.10.3 belongs to the explicitly unmaintained legacy line.

algo.reason: Algo is Ansible-based server deployment automation, not an installable desktop VPN client; a separate WireGuard client is not Algo.

spleeter.reason: Official stable distribution is PyPI/pip, which is not a supported schema-3 installation method.

cmder.reason: Stable 1.3.26 portable archives have no supported package mapping, Pakkit portable is Rufus-only, and current 2.x is prerelease.

chromium.reason: The complete distributed browser includes non-OSI IJG and legacy OpenSSL license components and cannot be represented by the root BSD-3-Clause alone.

bongocat.reason: The complete product vendors Live2D Cubism Core under a proprietary license and cannot be represented as Apache-2.0 alone.

spacemacs.reason: The distribution is a Git clone into .emacs.d rather than a supported package; bundled third-party material also includes non-OSI CC BY-SA terms.

piliplus.reason: A stable winget package exists but generic GPLv3 text and package metadata do not prove GPL-3.0-only versus GPL-3.0-or-later.
